cultura.name: El Tango
cultura.description:
UNESCO-listed embrace dance born in Buenos Aires immigrant tenements.
Intense, improvised, and intimate — tango is Argentina's soul in motion.

cultura.name: La Cultura Gaucha
cultura.description:
Horse-riding cowboys of the Pampas who shaped Argentine national identity.
Their equestrian skill, poncho, and folk songs echo through festivals today.

cultura.name: El Fútbol Argentino
cultura.description:
Football is a near-religion — home of Messi, Maradona, and La Albiceleste.
El Superclásico (Boca vs River) is one of the world's greatest sporting spectacles.

cultura.name: La Literatura Bonaerense

Home of Jorge Luis Borges, whose labyrinths and mirrors shaped world literature.
Buenos Aires has more bookshops per capita than any other city on Earth.

india_traveller.visa_note: Indian passport holders require a Tourist Visa (Visa de Turismo) for Argentina, obtained from the Argentine Consulate in Delhi or Mumbai. Apply 4–6 weeks in advance. No Schengen visa required — separate from Europe.
india_traveller.flight_note: No direct flights from India to Argentina. Common routes go via Dubai (Emirates), Doha (Qatar Airways), or São Paulo (LATAM). Total journey time is typically 20–26 hours. Buenos Aires Ezeiza (EZE) is the main international airport.
india_traveller.cost_per_day_inr: Budget travellers can manage on ₹2,500–4,000/day (hostels + local food). Mid-range trips cost ₹6,000–10,000/day. The peso exchange rate makes Argentina relatively affordable. Malbec wine and steak dinners are surprisingly pocket-friendly.
india_traveller.veg_tips: Argentina is a meat-heavy country, but vegetarian options are growing in Buenos Aires. Look for 'vegetariano' menus in San Telmo and Palermo. Locro (stew), empanadas de queso, medialunas, and salads are safe bets. Say: 'Soy vegetariano/a, sin carne por favor.'
